about: Guidance lines for seasonal tasks (PLAN.md section 7, low-impact guidance; P0-12). Each line is either cited, with a named publisher and a web address, or general, worded as general advice and naming no source it does not have. Numbers marked engineering_default are ours, not published, and are tuned from owner answers after one season.

xerces_stems.name: Xerces Society
xerces_stems.detail: Put down those pruners: pollinators need your garden garbage

msu_leaves_lawn.name: Michigan State University Extension
msu_leaves_lawn.detail: Mulch leaves into turf for a smart lawn (not yet read in full)

wrcc_freeze.name: Western Regional Climate Center
wrcc_freeze.detail: Freeze and frost classes (what a light, moderate and severe freeze does to plants)

general.name: General gardening advice
general.detail: No primary page is attached to this line yet, and sources differ.

frost_tender.text: Let tender annuals go at frost. Cover or bring in only the plants you want to keep.
frost_tender.low_impact_note: A light frost ends tender annuals; there is no need to protect everything.

frost_pots.text: Bring tender potted plants indoors or into a sheltered spot before the cold night. Roots in pots get colder than roots in the ground.

frost_info_woody.text: Trees, shrubs and lawn are not harmed by a light frost. Nothing to do for them.

freeze_water.text: General advice: in a dry autumn, water new plantings and evergreens until the ground freezes. Sources differ on how much.

hard_freeze_stems.text: A hard freeze ends the season for perennials. Leave their stems and seed heads standing over winter.
hard_freeze_stems.low_impact_note: Standing stems shelter overwintering insects and seed heads feed birds. Remove only plants that were diseased.

hardening_no_feed.text: General advice: skip fertilizer for trees, shrubs and garden beds from now until spring growth starts. It is not needed unless a soil test says otherwise. Sources differ on fall feeding.
hardening_no_feed.low_impact_note: Late feeding can push soft growth that winter kills. This is not lawn advice: cool-season lawns are often fed in early fall.

hardening_no_prune.text: General advice: hold off pruning trees and shrubs until they are dormant, apart from dead or broken branches.

leaves_beds.text: Leave whole leaves in garden beds and under trees and shrubs. Do not shred or bag them.
leaves_beds.low_impact_note: Leaf litter is free mulch and winter shelter for insects.

leaves_lawn.text: A thin layer of leaves on the lawn is fine: mow over a light covering, and rake thick mats into beds.
leaves_lawn.low_impact_note: Mowing destroys insects in those leaves, so mow only what is on the lawn and move the rest whole.

leaves_paths.text: General advice: clear leaves from paths, drains and gutters, and move them onto beds rather than to the curb.

dormant_woody.text: General advice: trees and shrubs are resting for winter. Late winter is a common time to prune most deciduous trees; wait to prune spring-flowering shrubs until after they bloom.

emergence_beds.text: New growth is starting. Leave last year's leaf cover in beds a little longer and look before you step in.

late_frost_cover.text: General advice: if frost is forecast after new growth starts, cover tender shoots and new plantings overnight, and wait to see what recovers before cutting anything back.

cleanup_stems.text: Now is late enough to tidy beds. Cut last year's stems down, leave the stubble standing for stem-nesting bees, and leave cut stems loosely piled rather than bagged.
cleanup_stems.low_impact_note: Waiting until late spring lets overwintering insects come out first.

tender_out.text: General advice: move tender potted plants back outside once nights stay mild, a few hours at first in shade.
